topic.title: Legal, regulatory & security risk

what.t: Bartz v. Anthropic: a court order (T1) gave final approval on Jul 20, 2026 to a non-reversionary $1.5B class settlement over 482,460 works, about $3,109 each (derived), with $101.56M in fees and dismissal with prejudice. The Jun 23, 2025 ruling held training fair use but the pirated library not. A T3 schedule puts $450M due Sep 25, 2027.

Suits followed the signing: Carreyrou opt-outs (Dec 22, 2025, T2), Concord II (Jan 28, 20,517 works, Amodei and Mann named), BMG (Mar 17, T2), Cognella and Chicken Soup (May), Round Hill (Aug 17), Sony and Warner Chappell (Aug 28). Concord I fair-use summary judgment is heard Oct 21. Reddit survived a demurrer on 3 of 5 claims Sep 17 (T3).

Pentagon: a Jan 9 memo demanded 'any lawful use'. Feb 27 directives and a Mar 3 FASCSA determination followed. N.D. Cal. enjoined Mar 26 and on Aug 27 vacated the 10 U.S.C. 3252 designation and contractor boycott (orders, T1). The D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion 2-1 on Sep 25, Henderson dissenting, mandate withheld (opinion, T1). Michael says Anthropic is still designated (Sep 3, T3).

A Commerce directive at 5:21pm ET on Jun 12 barred foreign nationals from Fable 5 and Mythos 5. Anthropic disabled both worldwide (Anthropic, T1; BIS per CSIS, T2). Mythos 5 was partly approved Jun 26, controls lifted Jun 30, Fable 5 restored Jul 1. On Sep 24 the National Cyber Director's office asked Anthropic to hold Mythos 5.1 from UK AISI; it complied (Politico, T2).

Anthropic's Nov 13, 2025 report said a Chinese state-sponsored group ran 80-90% of an espionage campaign on about 30 targets via Claude Code (company claim, T1). Its Sep 10 report adds Russian and Chinese espionage and about 200M distillation exchanges, Alibaba 151M on 3,500 accounts. The June letter said Alibaba 28.8M on about 25,000 accounts (DISPUTED). CISA, FBI and NSA named six Chinese firms Sep 8 (T1).

Anthropic disclosed three incidents on Jul 30 and a fourth, from January, on Sep 9 (T1) in which Claude models accessed real systems; Mythos 5's malicious PyPI package ran on 15 systems. The FTC opened a probe of Anthropic, OpenAI and METR on agentic AI on Sep 30, citing the Jul 30 breaches (Reuters via Yahoo, T2, single source, first reported by the New York Post).

means.t: Bartz held training on lawfully acquired books fair use and piracy not. Exposure turns on how data was obtained, priced per work up to $150,000. The $1.5B releases past conduct on listed works and is no licence for future training. It is one-time for that class but recurs class by class, since most new complaints plead the same piracy theory. Reddit's contract claims sit outside fair use.

Two instruments produced two outcomes. N.D. Cal. vacated the 10 U.S.C. 3252 designation and the contractor boycott on First Amendment, due-process and APA grounds. The D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion, finding Anthropic's refusal of 'all lawful uses', not its speech, caused it. Defense and Defense Industrial Base use stays excluded. Civil-agency eligibility is restored unless the government wins on appeal.

The June directive was a letter with no specifics or process. Nationality could not be verified in real time, so Anthropic shut both models for all users. Restoration required cyber classifiers with an Opus 4.8 fallback, pre-release government access and malicious-activity reporting. Both Mythos-class launches (Jun 9, Sep 1) drew federal action, the Jun 12 recall and the Sep 24 hold. Four other launches drew none in the record.

Dollar exposure exists only where a per-unit formula does. Copyright has one, statutory damages per work, so 2 of 39 rows carry a liability figure: Bartz $1.5B and Concord II's theoretical $3B. Government actions have no price, and the Pentagon's only figure is Anthropic's own declaration. Pentagon, export, FTC and security matters hit access and revenue, so they show up as lost customers, delays and disclosure.

implications.t: Model the $1.5B as a one-time charge for listed works and copyright as serial claims. Reference class: Bartz, the only settlement in the record, at $3,109 per work, 2.1% of the statutory maximum (derived). On 35,874 counted music works that is about $112M, against $5.4B at the ceiling (derived). Sony and Warner Chappell counts are not in the record. Re-mark after Oct 21.

Treat Pentagon workload revenue as largely lost and commercial spillover as contingent. The March declaration sized 2026 revenue risk at hundreds of millions to multiple billions when run-rate was $14B (T1, gross) to $19B (T3). Run-rate is $65B now (T2, gross), and Judge Lin vacated the contractor boycott. The Pentagon says about 90% of workloads moved, though NSA use of Mythos is reported (T3).

Top two by dollars: music suits (ceiling $5.4B) and the Pentagon declaration (multiple billions, uncapped). Then Bartz cash due ($450M) and opt-outs (ceiling $270M). Bartz, music and opt-out figures sum to about $7.2B, 0.74% of the $965B mark (ceilings and sums derived). By timing: FTC probe, D.C. Circuit review, Oct 21 hearing, METR report. The S-1 is not yet public (T1); check it covers all four.

Likely risk-factor topics, by cases-table notes: Bartz, music, publisher and opt-out suits, Reddit, the Pentagon label, the June recall, the FTC probe, eval incidents, distillation. Among these, press confirms only self-preservation, agentic legal risk and (T4, VERIFY) backlash language. Treat recall and hold power as an operating risk. Check the S-1 for Commerce's reported right to reimpose restrictions (T4) and SB 53 incident reporting.

second_order: Valuation is now a litigation input. Concord II pleaded a $350B+ valuation and Sony and Warner Chappell pleaded $965B, arguing $1.5B does not deter. A listing near $2T (WSJ, T3) hands the next plaintiff a larger anchor, so per-work asks may track market cap. Underwriters, insurers and counsel must price that. Consensus may treat Bartz as a ceiling; plaintiffs cite it as a floor.

The Pentagon dispute may end by politics, not judgment. The rulings rest on different statutes and courts, and Anthropic is considering further review with no deadline in the record. Meanwhile Lutnick signals the security rift is over (Sep 2, T3), Trump and Amodei dined Sep 27 (date inferred), and Amodei signed the Sep 29 voluntary pact. Consensus watches the courts; the lever may be the White House.

Regulators converge on one capability. Commerce (recall), the National Cyber Director (hold), the FTC (developer liability, single source), the Pentagon (exclusion), the EU (watermarking from Aug 2) and California (SB 53 incident reports) all act on cyber-capable agents. OpenAI is named beside Anthropic in the FTC probe and the hold, so the burden is sector-wide: a timing risk for a crowded IPO window, not a relative discount.

Security events now cross into legal and policy. UTRF's Jul 20 patent complaint cites internal Claude Code file names such as autoDream.ts, which the record infers came from the Mar 31 leak. Distillation claims drive policy asks, yet Alibaba account counts differ about 7x (derived) between the June letter and the September report, over different windows. Challenged counts would weaken the tailwind.

Advocacy has become a liability. Amodei's Sep 12 pacing essay is cited in the Buist antitrust complaint (Sep 18), Sacks called the push regulatory capture (Sep 13, T3), and WSJ (T3) ties the November slip to scrutiny after the CEO's pace warnings. A safety-first stance now carries antitrust and timing cost. Consensus may treat the policy stance as brand; the record shows legal and IPO consequences.

watch.item: Reddit refile deadline for the unjust-enrichment and trespass claims dismissed with leave (SF Superior, Judge Kahn)
watch.threshold: Refiling restores 5 of 5 claims. No refiling leaves 3 contract-based claims, which fair use does not reach.

watch.item: Concord I cross-motions for summary judgment on lyric fair use, 10:00 AM, San Jose Courtroom 7 (Judge Lee)
watch.threshold: A ruling that lyric training or outputs are not fair use would reprice Concord II, Round Hill, Sony and Warner Chappell and BMG and likely draw new filings; at least 10 have followed the Bartz signing (derived). A fair-use win narrows them to the piracy theory. Ruling date is not in the record.

watch.item: D.C. Circuit follow-up: Anthropic's choice on en banc rehearing or certiorari (mandate withheld), the government's stayed Ninth Circuit appeal 26-2011, and DoD phase-out completion (Sep 30 per FedScoop, end of October per DefenseScoop)
watch.threshold: A filing, a grant or a Ninth Circuit order. Deadlines are not in the record. A government appeal of the Aug 27 judgment would reopen the commercial-boycott risk.

watch.item: FTC formal information demands and compelled executive testimony on agentic AI risk
watch.threshold: Demands served on Anthropic or named executives, or an FTC statement on developer liability for test-induced hacks. No dates are in the record.

watch.item: Public S-1 on EDGAR: Item 103 legal proceedings and litigation risk factors
watch.threshold: Text covers Bartz appeals, music suits, Reddit, the FASCSA loss, the FTC probe and the four eval incidents, and states any accrual or range of loss. A missing item is a disclosure gap.

watch.item: METR independent investigation of the four eval incidents (eight-week agreement, extendable, reported Sep 9)
watch.threshold: Date is derived from Sep 9 plus eight weeks, start date unconfirmed. Findings of further incidents, or an extension past early November, would need S-1 disclosure.

watch.item: Bartz: first distribution due on or before Nov 15; Ninth Circuit 26-5455 opening brief Nov 12, answering brief Dec 14; confirmation that the $450M due Sep 25, 2026 was paid
watch.threshold: Distribution starts on time and no appeal blocks the Effective Date. A late objector appeal (Dkt 687) that survives would delay finality.

watch.item: Federal action on model availability or on distillers: Treasury or Commerce listing Moonshot or Alibaba, or a further hold or recall of a Mythos-class model
watch.threshold: A formal designation would back the distillation case. A third availability action in 2026 would make recall risk a pattern. None found as of Sep 30.

topic.house_view: (a) Extends: 16 open court matters, an upheld Pentagon exclusion and a new FTC probe sit beside a $965B Series H mark and a reported $2T target with no legal discount mentioned in the record, though this slice holds no multiples and so does not test the belief. (b) Does not apply, except that the CFO's revenue-at-risk figures state no gross or net basis. (c) Extends: dated legal catalysts add issuer-specific timing risk to pipeline risk, and the window has already slid to mid-October (Reuters Sep 4, T3), November (WSJ Sep 18, T3) and after the midterms (Reuters Sep 29, T2). (d) No direct test: the record does not say how the $1.5B is funded, and if equity paid it, the equity-raised denominator carries $1.5B that bought no capacity. (e) Confirms in part: per-work statutory damages on training data and a federal recall of a live model within hours are frontier-lab exposures that software-sector legal conventions would miss.

uncertainties.note: The prospectus tables (risk_factor_themes, prospectus_facts, offering_structure) are empty. Opened coverage of the leaked S-1 (TechCrunch, T2; Reuters via Crunchbase, T3) gives about 80 risk-factor pages but omits legal proceedings. Which matters appear in risk factors is inferred from press summaries and cases-table notes, not read from the filing.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A public S-1 on EDGAR, or a full read of the Reuters and FT reviews.

uncertainties.note: The cases table lags events. It omits BMG, the Carreyrou opt-out suit, the Sep 30 FTC probe, the Sep 24 hold and the Jul 1 FTC bias statement, and still shows Reddit as unverified after the Sep 17 ruling. Rows bundle dockets. Two events carry notes for unrelated merged items, so the opt-out author suits, a Legion LegalTech suit over the export order and the Bartz fee appeals have no event of their own. The count of 16 open court matters is a floor.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A cases-table refresh and un-merged event ids.

uncertainties.note: Music exposure is a bound, not an estimate. Reference class: one AI copyright settlement in the record, Bartz at about $3,109 per work or 2.1% of the statutory maximum, n=1, no other base rate. Different here: a lyrics fair-use ruling is pending Oct 21, anti-circumvention and model-weight claims are pleaded, and founders are named. The Dec 2023 customer copyright indemnity could route output claims to Anthropic; the record shows no claim and no cap.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The Oct 21 ruling, or any music-suit settlement.

uncertainties.note: Pentagon exposure rests on litigation declarations, not audited revenue, and states no gross or net basis. The range was written when run-rate was $14B (T1, gross) to $19B (T3, basis unstated). Realized loss is not in the record beyond the Pentagon's claim that about 90% of workloads moved (T2). Reference class: none in the record, since the label had never been applied to a US company.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: S-1 disclosure of public-sector and defense-related revenue.

uncertainties.note: Bartz cash is unverified. The installment schedule comes from the Authors Guild (T3), payment of the $450M due Sep 25, 2026 is not confirmed, the floor is at least $1.5B plus interest, and a late objector notice (Dkt 687) leaves the Effective Date uncertain. No accrual or reserve for any matter appears in the record.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Administrator or docket confirmation of payment and the Effective Date, or S-1 disclosure of accruals.

Counted categories: legal 65, regulatory 40, security 45 events; 134 in the union.

q.py --cat regulatory: read all 40 headlines and summaries.
q.py --cat security: read all 45 headlines and summaries.
q.py --table cases: read all 39 rows (18 litigation, 9 regulatory, 5 security, 7 controversy).
Checked metrics tables risk_factor_themes, prospectus_facts, offering_structure: all empty, so the risk-factor ranking is inference.
q.py --conflicts and --open with keywords (Bartz, settlement, FASCSA, export, distill, Alibaba, Reddit, Concord, FTC, SB 53, prospectus, appeal): read ledger conflicts and open items for my slice.
q.py --cat government,policy --from 2026-01-01; --cat ipo --from 2026-05-01; --cat model --from 2026-05-01: headline reads for Pentagon, IPO-timing and launch-base-rate context.
Bartz fair-use order Jun 23, 2025: training fair use, 7M+ pirated copies not, trial set on damages.
Bartz settlement signed Sep 5, 2025: $1.5B, 482,460 works, non-reversionary, installments per Authors Guild (T3).
Bartz final approval Jul 20, 2026: fees $101.56M, 350 opt-outs covering 1,802 works, judgment, dismissal with prejudice.
Per-work math: $1.5B / 482,460 = $3,109, matching the record's 'about $3,000' and '$3,100' as rounding. Fees $101.56M = 6.8% of the fund.

Ledger conflicts on Bartz: fees $101.56M (order) versus about $122M (TechTimes, which adds expenses and cost reserve), 482,460 versus about 500,000 works, opt-out deadline Feb 9 versus Jan 29. All resolved to the court order.
Objections: 53 at the May 14 hearing (Courthouse News, T2/MEDIUM) versus 54 overruled in the final order (T1). Final order used.
Bartz cash unverified: $450M due Sep 25, 2026 not confirmed (schedule is Authors Guild T3); docket shows only a Sep 29 clerk notice; late objector notice Dkt 687.
Concord I: preliminary injunction denied Mar 25, 2025; cross-motions for summary judgment heard Oct 21, 2026 (10:00 AM, San Jose).
Concord II filed Jan 28, 2026: 20,517 works, Amodei and Mann named, pleads $350B+ valuation.
Publisher suits after the Bartz signing: BMG Mar 17, Cognella May 4, Chicken Soup May 7, Round Hill Aug 17, Sony and Warner Chappell Aug 28 (pleads $965B valuation).
Statutory arithmetic: 20,517 x $150,000 = $3.08B matches the record; 35,874 counted music works = $5.4B at ceiling, $112M at the Bartz rate (derived).

Merge artifact: evt-20260422 (Concord I) carries notes for six unrelated merged items (D.C. Cir. stay, Reddit remand, Kwon/Cruz/Shakespeare opt-outs, Legion LegalTech v. US over the export order, D.C. Cir. petition 26-1162). Four have no event of their own.
Merge artifact: evt-20260922 (Kahn motion to dismiss) holds the merged Bartz fee and objector appeals notes (9th Cir. 25-4843, 26-5391, 26-5455).
Reddit: sued Jun 4, 2025, remanded Mar 2026, Sep 17 demurrer overruled on contract, interference and UCL; refile deadline Oct 16.
Stale table: cases row for Reddit says status not verified, but the event record shows the Sep 17, 2026 demurrer ruling (T3).

Coverage gap: cases table omits BMG (Mar 17), Carreyrou opt-outs (Dec 22, 2025), FTC probe (Sep 30), FTC bias statement (Jul 1), Australian Senate (Sep 27) and the Sep 24 hold. The open count is a floor.
q.py --q 'Department of War', --q Pentagon (from Apr 1), --q Lutnick: read Pentagon context events outside my categories.
Pentagon origin: Jan 9 'any lawful use' memo, Jan 29 impasse, Feb 26 Amodei refusal, Feb 27 directives, Mar 3 FASCSA determination.
CFO declaration Mar 9: hundreds of millions to multiple billions of 2026 revenue at risk, three deals over $180M collapsed, 50-100% of DoW-related revenue.
N.D. Cal. Aug 27: summary judgment, 3252 designation and secondary boycott vacated, permanent injunction; ultra vires claim lost.
D.C. Circuit Sep 25: petitions denied 2-1 (Katsas, Rao; Henderson dissenting); mandate withheld; Anthropic 'considering all options'.
Cross-checked cases rows 16 and 17 against events: Aug 27 and Sep 25 dates, statutes (3252 versus 41 U.S.C. 4713) and outcomes agree.

Scale check against run_rate_desk: $14B gross (Feb 12, T1), $19B basis unstated (Mar 3, T3), $65B gross (end July, T2). Bartz is about 33% of FY2025 revenue (about $4.6B, leaked S-1) but 2.3% of the $65B run-rate and 0.16% of the $965B mark. Bases differ: recognized revenue versus annualized run-rate.
DoD phase-out end date differs: Sep 29 (MeriTalk), Sep 30 (FedScoop), end of October (DefenseScoop Sep 11), or 180 days from the CIO memo.
CIO removal memo is dated Mar 5 in one event and Mar 6 in another (and in the cases table).
Michael's Sep 3 post cites 10 U.S.C. 3252 per Unite.AI (T3, single source), the designation Judge Lin vacated Aug 27. Possible compliance friction, unverified.
Workloads moved: about 2/3 (MeriTalk, cited in the cases table) versus about 90% (Michael, Sep 11). Different dates, moving number.
NSA (a DoW agency) is reported using Mythos (Axios Apr 20, FT Jun 5, both T3) while DoW calls Anthropic a supply-chain risk; Judge Lin questioned this Jul 30. The exclusion is not uniform.
Dec 2023 copyright indemnity for API customers is an unquantified contingent liability: no claim and no cap in the record, and no accrual for any matter.
Export directive Jun 12, 5:21pm ET; Jun 26 partial approval; Jun 30 lifted; Jul 1 restored; conditions and 50% weekly-limit promotion to Jul 7.
Outage length is 18 days (Anthropic, Jun 12 to Jun 30) or 19 (calendar to Jul 1). Partial-approval date is Jun 26 (Anthropic) or Jun 27 (MeriTalk). Both kept.
Issuing agency for the Jun 12 directive is not named by Anthropic; BIS per CSIS and Harvard Law Review blog (T2); open item in the ledger.
Base rate on availability actions: Mythos-class launches Jun 9 and Sep 1 both drew a federal action; Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 drew none in the record (n=2).
Sep 24: White House asks labs to hold Mythos 5.1 from UK AISI; Anthropic complied; Mythos 5.1 already limited to US verified organizations.
Eval incidents: three disclosed Jul 30 (Opus 4.7, Mythos 5, internal model), overhaul Aug 31, fourth (January) Sep 9; 141,006 runs reviewed, 481M transcripts scanned.
Mythos 5 package ran on '15 systems' (Jul 30, T1) versus 'infected 15 security vendors' (Sep 9 note). Fourth incident disclosed Sep 9 (T1) versus a Sep 10 Reuters headline. T1 used.
SB 53 requires critical-incident reports within 15 days; the January incident surfaced Sep 9 and no state filing is recorded. Ledger open item.
Distillation: Feb 23 (16M exchanges, about 24,000 accounts), Jun 10 Alibaba letter, Jul 22 Moonshot and Treasury threat, Sep 8 CISA advisory AA26-251A, Sep 10 report (about 200M).
DISPUTED: Alibaba 28.8M exchanges on about 25,000 accounts (Jun 10 letter, Apr 22 to Jun 5) versus 151M on 3,500 accounts (Sep report, May to Jul). Both named; no side picked.
An Alibaba v. DoD suit (5:26-cv-06227, Jun 23) is noted inside an Alibaba distillation event with relation unverified.
Mythos CMS leak appears twice: Mar 1 (T3, month precision) and Mar 26 (T2, Fortune). Likely one incident; counted once.
Cases row 38 calls forgone China-linked revenue unquantified; the Feb 26 Amodei statement note says 'several hundred million dollars' (company claim).
FTC probe Sep 30 (T2, single source) and S-1 status: confidential Jun 1, leak Sep 28-29 with about 80 risk-factor pages, no public S-1 on EDGAR.

Legal-proceedings content of the S-1 is unverified; opened coverage, including the new desk-s1 event, omits it. Listing window slid: mid-October (Reuters Sep 4, T3), November (WSJ Sep 18, T3), after midterms (Reuters Sep 29, T2).
Open-matter count from cases rows: 18 litigation rows = 16 open (13 defendant, 3 plaintiff) + 1 settled + 1 closed. Only 2 of 39 rows carry a liability dollar figure.

Shared record regenerated at 18:41 (662 events, legal 66, desk-s1 and desk-revenue merged). Re-checked every cited id, tier and the cases table; one id changed to evt-20260817-rr-65b-end-july; one new slice event (desk-s1 prospectus).

Ranking is by record-supported ceilings and dated catalysts only; Pentagon and music figures are bounds with no base rate beyond Bartz (n=1).
